client_brief:
Help us prepare Ada's family photographs for the reunion

Hello,

We are putting together photographs for the Hollis family reunion at Thanksgiving. Nine older scans need careful preparation for printing and sharing. We would like them to sit together, but we do not want the photographs modernised or the people changed.

Some fading and differences between the originals are part of their history. Please make a considered decision about what can be improved, and leave a short note where the source puts a limit on the result. Nothing should be invented to fill a damaged or missing part of a photograph.

This is what we would like back:

Nine photographs from four decades brought to one archival target (one paper white, one black point, one degree of correction, one crop logic), levelled where levelling is honest, fade recovered and cast corrected where the print has actually shifted, with nothing invented and nothing that is genuinely in the scan removed. Delivered as A4 proportioned framing files and smaller share renditions, every output at or below its source dimensions, plus one licensed camera-scale cover ground graded into the same set, with a per photograph parameter log and one line on why each differs.

A proof set on the real light and dark destination grounds, including full-resolution edge inspections, delivery-size previews, and explicit pass/fail notes. It must reference Ada Hollis restored archive, nine photographs plus one licensed cover ground and function as approval evidence rather than decoration.

Our files: hollis_scans/ (9 flatbed scans, approx 2200 x 3000 to 4000 x 5200); mountcard_2019_print.pdf; photo_catalogue.csv; family_notes.txt.

Please make the print and smaller sharing versions easy for the family to tell apart. The final checks should be made at the sizes we will use, including against light and dark surroundings.

The commission is budgeted at $900-$2,400 fixed. We have allowed 7 to 15 business days, including one technical proof and two consolidated revision rounds. New deliverable classes, new source creation, extra records, and client copy changes after approval are quoted separately.

Handover: a delivery manifest, the editable sources specified above, final exports and a short production and exceptions note. Include an inventory showing how every supplied file was used or why it was set aside. Keep factual content tied to the approved inputs. Any missing coverage, substituted asset, reconciliation or quality compromise must be declared; a weak source is not permission to invent or silently replace it.

source_provenance.original_anchor: Primary anchor: the Freelancer.com posting 'Old Picture Restoration' (30 to 250 USD), whose client writes 'I need a physical photo restored. This is a personal keepsake and means a lot to me.' and lists 'Restore colors, details, and sharpness.' plus 'Experience with color correction and detail enhancement.' Co-anchor: the Freelancer.com brief from an individual with several old photo scans to restore 'for A4 printing to mount on my wall', naming colour fading as the damage. The killed spec sat on one surface and leaned on scratch and tear repair, which is generative healing and does not exist here; it was also a single atomic grade. The fuller commission this family genuinely has is the whole wall: the restoration, the framer's caption cards (a true record per page run rebuildable from the press file he left behind), and the keepsake folio they will keep editing after we go. Names, town and family are invented for this benchmark.

price_band_and_audience: A private heritage commission of 650 to 1,600 dollars, paid by three siblings in their sixties on behalf of twenty two family members aged 8 to 74, hung in a family house rather than sold to anyone. The band is load-bearing in an unusual direction: the money buys restraint, not effect. At this band the correct answer is a true archival neutral, deep honest blacks, one photograph per folio page, generous margins, a caption voice that reads like a museum label, and visible respect for the grain and the paper the print is actually made of. The same brief bought for 60 dollars from an online memory book service would correctly be warmer, brighter, collaged full bleed, set in a script face with drop shadows and a heart on the cover, and shipping that here is a failure the family will feel personally rather than commercially. Pushed the other way into a heavy sepia wash or a gallery black ground it becomes a stranger's idea of an old photograph, which is the other way to lose this job. Anything that reads as enhanced fails regardless of execution.

brand_identity.sector: A private family archive of one woman, Ada Hollis, restored and framed for a home wall and a keepsake folio, not sold to anyone.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Assembled in 2026 at the family house in Vermont, New England, by three siblings in their sixties acting on behalf of twenty two relatives.
brand_identity.about: The archive holds nine photographs of Ada Hollis, who died in April at ninety nine, spanning roughly 1912 to 1974. It exists so that twenty two people who come home at Thanksgiving can hang one wall of her and carry one folio each. The standard is a museum label, not a memory book: honest, quiet, and true to what is actually in the photograph.
brand_identity.audience: Three siblings commissioning on behalf of twenty two family members aged 8 to 74. Not a commercial audience: the work hangs in a family house and is judged by people who knew Ada.
brand_identity.price_positioning: A private heritage commission of 650 to 1,600 dollars. The money buys restraint rather than effect: a true archival neutral, deep honest blacks, one photograph per page, generous margins, and visible respect for the grain and the paper each print is made of.
brand_identity.typography: A quiet text serif set the way a museum sets a wall label: small, calm, well leaded, with a restrained display cut for the folio cover and course of names. Nothing decorative, no script, no drop shadow.
brand_identity.voice: Spare and factual, the voice of a caption card rather than a scrapbook. Example line the brand would write: "Ada Hollis, Brattleboro, 1912. Studio card portrait."
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: There are no brand files. What survives is nine home flatbed scans, the daughter's catalogue and notes, and the Brattleboro framer's 2019 press PDF for the caption cards, of which six are already on the wall. The framer has retired, so the new cards must match his file rather than a live template.
brand_identity.values: Identity is the whole point: whatever is really in the photograph stays in the photograph, and nothing is invented or tidied away.

assets_supplied.name: hollis_scans/ (9 flatbed scans, approx 2200 x 3000 to 4000 x 5200)
assets_supplied.kind: Home flatbed scans of nine photographs Ada kept, spanning roughly 1912 to 1974: studio card portraits, two mid century black and white prints, and four drugstore colour prints from the sixties and seventies.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Nine photographs of Nan, scanned at home by my brother. Some are faded, some have gone a strange colour, a couple are crooked."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Four of the nine were scanned still inside their album mounts or their deckled paper borders, and in those the picture sits a degree or two off level inside a mount that is itself perfectly square to the scanner glass, so an automatic level locks to the mount edge, reports success, returns a file, and the readout is that nothing has moved. Two of the colour prints have lost most of one dye layer, and which way each one's residual cast runs is not legible while the fade is still on it: the cast only becomes visible once the fade has been lifted and contrast is back, and the two run in opposite directions from each other.

assets_supplied.name: mountcard_2019_print.pdf
assets_supplied.kind: The Brattleboro framer's flat press PDF for the caption cards, A6 landscape, fonts embedded, produced from a real page layout so it converts cleanly. Carries a title line, a date and place line, a names line, a provenance line in italic, and a small placed reference thumbnail.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The card he ran for us in 2019. Six of these are already on the wall and the new ones have to match them."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: He drew the caption block around the captions he actually had in 2019, which were two or three words long, and it is a fixed measure frame in a document that does not spill and does not warn: a longer caption simply stops rendering at the frame edge, so a record carrying three names and a place loses its last name and its year at trim while the screen proof still looks like a finished card. What the conversion exposes as addressable structure is a property of how he built that document and is announced nowhere, and the italic provenance line sits as its own run inside a single continuous flow rather than as its own frame.

assets_supplied.name: photo_catalogue.csv
assets_supplied.kind: The spreadsheet Ada's daughter has kept for years, one row per photograph, with columns for caption title, date and place, names, provenance and a photo filename.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "What we know about each one. My aunt has kept this list going since the nineties."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Two rows are the same photograph, sent to her twice under different filenames by two cousins with slightly different dates, and shipping both puts a duplicate card on a wall that has a fixed number of frames. One row's date contradicts what is written on the back of that print, which appears in the family notes and not in the spreadsheet, and one row's photo column names a file that does not exist anywhere because the family renamed that scan after this export was taken.

assets_supplied.name: family_notes.txt
assets_supplied.kind: Two pages typed by Ada's daughter: what is written on the backs of the prints, who is in each photograph, which town each was taken in, and the things that must not be tidied away.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Everything we know, and the things we do not want touched."

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the automatic level actually moved the picture. Four of the nine were scanned inside their album mounts or their paper borders, and in those the strongest straight edges in the frame belong to the mount, which is square to the glass, while the photograph sits a degree or two off inside it. The call succeeds, a file comes back, and on those frames it is the file that went in. There is no angle readout, no rotation parameter and no measurement anywhere in the connector, and at thumbnail scale a two degree tilt inside a square mount and a levelled picture look the same, so the only way to learn which frames actually moved is to level them and compare what returned against what went in.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) No ordering avoids it and no care prevents it, because the tool takes no options and exposes no reference: what it locked onto is only observable afterwards. (b) Nothing states it. The brief says a couple are crooked and asks for the tilt corrected, which is the client's goal, and no asset note, no deliverable and no earlier step says anything about mounts or borders. (c) It is not a propagation re-run, because re-running the same call on the same frame returns the same file. The response is a different instrument and a real decision about how much of the mount is evidence worth keeping.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Confirm the unmoved frames by comparing return against input rather than by trusting the call, then isolate the picture area inside the mount and crop to it before levelling again, decide per photograph whether the deckled border stays as part of the object or goes, and re-derive that photograph's framing crop and its caption card thumbnail from the corrected master.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Four of the nine hang visibly crooked on a wall built for one woman, next to five that are level, in front of twenty two people who asked for exactly this and were told it was done.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Which way each faded colour print's residual cast actually runs. Two of the drugstore prints have lost most of one dye layer, and while the fade is still on them both simply read as generically yellowed at any scale: the cast is masked by the missing contrast. Only once the fade is lifted and the tonal range is back does the true bias appear, and on these two it appears in opposite directions, so a neutralisation that visibly rescues one drives the other further off. With no eyedropper and no histogram, the recovery is the diagnostic, and it can only be read by looking at what came back.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) Ordering cannot avoid it, since the fade must be lifted before the cast is legible, and care cannot settle it, because two prints that look identically yellowed as supplied are not carrying the same fault. (b) Nothing states it. The brief says the sixties and seventies prints have gone a strange colour and asks for the colour corrected, which is the goal; no asset note names dye layers or directions. (c) It is not a propagation re-run: the response is a different correction on one of the two, taken in the opposite direction from the one that worked, and then a fresh judgement of both against the seven others.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Correct each of the two on its own evidence rather than by copying the move that worked, re-judge both against the black and white masters, and decide whether either has been pushed to where it no longer reads as a print of its decade, which the family has ruled out. Any change here re-flows into that photograph's framing file, its share rendition and its card thumbnail.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Half the colour prints on the wall sit visibly green or magenta beside the others, which is precisely the thing the family said was wrong with them in the first place, delivered back as finished restoration work.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether every caption actually reaches the printed card. The framer drew the caption block around the captions he had in 2019, which were two or three words, and it is a fixed measure frame: text that runs past it does not spill, does not reflow and does not warn, it simply stops at the frame edge. The merge reports success, the page count equals the row count, the validator was happy and the proof at screen scale reads as a finished card, because a caption that stops after two of three names still looks like a caption. Whether THIS catalogue's longest rows fit THAT frame is a property of the framer's document and cannot be known before the cards are rendered at trim and read.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) Ordering cannot avoid it and nothing in the merge chain reports overset, so an agent doing everything correctly still cannot learn it before rendering. (b) Nothing states it. The brief asks for one card per photograph matching the 2019 set, which is the goal, and the acceptance line about complete captions is the family's own standing requirement, not a disclosure that a specific record overflows. (c) It is not a propagation re-run: the fix is an editorial and typographic decision (shorten the caption, split the names onto the line the framer left for them, or accept a smaller size on one line) taken against six cards already hanging that cannot be changed.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Read every rendered card at trim rather than at proof scale, identify which records are losing content, then re-cut those captions or re-assign content between the framer's existing lines so nothing is lost, re-merge, re-render and re-read, and record in the note which caption wording was changed and why so the family is not surprised by it on the wall.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A card goes into a frame beside six from 2019 with a woman's married name and the year simply missing, printed, mounted and hung, discovered by the family at Thanksgiving rather than by us.

decision_gates: What is damage to correct and what is the age of the object to preserve, on prints where grain, paper texture and a studio retoucher's pencil work are all present.
Whether an automatic level actually moved a given picture, and how much of an album mount or a deckled border is evidence worth keeping when it did not.
Which way each faded colour print's residual cast runs, when both read identically yellowed as supplied and no measurement exists anywhere.
How far a fade recovery can be taken before the print stops looking like a print of its decade, at a band where anything that reads as enhanced fails.
One archival target for four decades and four papers, and which photograph, if any, cannot be brought to it.
The catalogue: one photograph entered twice, one date contradicted by the back of the print, one photo reference pointing at a renamed file. What is the agent's call and what is the family's.
Whether to trust the mapping tool's readout of the framer's text or to reconstruct the story independently from the document.
Whether per-photograph identity is established by position in a returned list or by opening the file.

why_not_vlm: Paste the brief and the scans into a frontier image model and it returns a beautiful old photograph of a woman who is not Ada Hollis. IDENTITY is the entire commission: a generative restore invents the eyes, the hairline, the teeth and the hand, and this family has already told us in writing what happened the last time somebody improved their grandmother. Every corrected pixel must derive from the pixels in the scan. SPEC: the family needs one A6 caption card per catalogued photograph matching six already hanging, complete at trim, with per-photograph files each containing the photograph they claim, and proofs at true print resolution. EDITABILITY: the folio is defined by being editable, because the aunt will find three more names. And the middle of the engagement is verification against material reality: did this level actually move the picture, which way does this cast run once the fade is lifted, does this caption reach the edge of the card.
